sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Save and read preferences handlers
sections.what: POST saves onboarding choices to the account when signed in and sets language and sports cookies. GET returns the signed-in user's saved choices.
sections.why: Likely reason: the cookies let visitors keep choices before signing up.
sections.watch_out: The language cookie name is typed here as text, while the language route imports it from the i18n provider, so renaming it needs both changed.

summary: Saves onboarding choices such as language and sports. Signed-in fans keep them on their account. Everyone gets them as cookies. A signed-in fan can read them back.
purpose: Remembers the choices a fan makes when they first set up the app.
why: The comment says choices are saved on the account when signed in and as cookies for everyone, so they work before sign-up.
how: POST: 1) Checks the body. 2) Saves to the account if signed in. 3) Sets language and sports cookies for a year. GET: 1) Requires sign-in. 2) Returns the saved preferences.
inputs: A POST with the preference choices. A GET with the session.
outputs: The saved preferences as JSON, plus two cookies.
risks: Anonymous visitors cannot read back their saved choices, so they rely on the cookies alone.
debug: If preferences do not save, check the preferences input shape and the save function in the users service.
